notes:
Top-line: mid-market SaaS (product onboarding copilots). Evaluating Hosted API first — want to prove latency SLOs and token cost caps — then move to Dedicated for predictable latency/cost.

Call notes:
- Product lead (Avery) and Engineering (Sam) on call. Focus: streaming for in-app chat, tool-calls to lookup user state, deterministic response times for flows.
- Quote from Avery: "Users drop off when first-run onboarding takes >1s to respond. We need consistent snappy replies."
- POC results: Hosted API hit p50 targets easily; p95 regressed when tool-calls (external DB lookup) happened — likely queuing/batching interactions.
- Cost: session token cap requirement — want ability to cap tokens per session and get estimated per-session spend. Current target cap: ~$0.20/session average. Very cost-sensitive.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration & US/EU residency (data residency flagged).
- Ops ask: per-route dashboards (latency, token consumption) and alerting for quality regressions.
- Proposed next steps: 7-day Dedicated POC with reserved capacity demo, pricing quote for 12-mo commit, and legal/sec deep-dive.
- Quotes/actions: Jordan to send dedicated sizing + price band, Maya to run latency breakdown with kernel/core telemetry, legal to review drive doc (referenced).
- Internal note: good fit for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + caching) to hit cost target without sacrificing latency.
requirements_summary: Workload: chat/agent for in-app onboarding. Latency SLOs: p50 < 250ms, p95 target < 800-1000ms (hard requirement for top flows). Must support streaming responses and function/tool calling for stateful lookups. Enforce per-session token caps and provide per-route cost telemetry. Model preference: open or Redwood-verified models with function-calling + streaming; able to fallback to smaller variant on capacity constraints. Deployment: start hosted API POC, then migrate to Dedicated reserved pool for consistent p95. Security: SSO/SAML, audit logging, KMS key control, EU/US data residency.
